meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law Foundation with Strong Common Law Statutory Influences in Corporate and Commercial Matters

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 on AML/CFT, as amended by Ley 70 de 2019; Decreto Ejecutivo 461 de 2015 (implementing regulations); Ley 129 de 8 de diciembre de 2020 establishing the Beneficial Owner Registry (Registro de Personas Jurídicas); Acuerdo No. 5-2020 of the Dirección General del Registro Público; Ley 52 de 2016 (FATCA IGA) and Decreto Ejecutivo 379 de 2017 (CRS adoption); regulations and guidelines issued by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Intendencia de Sujetos No Financieros.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Escritura Pública / Acta Constitutiva de la Sociedad Anónima)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama together with the incorporating attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a Contracting State since May 14, 2008)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Legal Existence (Certificado de Personería Jurídica)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Dirección General del Registro Público de Panamá
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille when used abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Power of Attorney (Poder General o Especial)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP classification and enhanced due diligence under Ley 23 de 2015, UAF guidelines and Decree 461 of 2015; continuous screening of shareholders, directors, officers and beneficial owners against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Council Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Sanctions List and Panama's national sanctions/aligned lists; mandatory EDD for PEPs from Latin America, the Caribbean, and high-risk jurisdictions; automatic re-screening triggers upon banking onboarding (Mercury, Wise) and material ownership changes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Act No. 32 of 26 February 1927, as amended), Titles I–IV (formation, shares, directors); Executive Decree No. 3 of 2017 (electronic registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Division (Dirección de Personas Jurídicas)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Incorporation Deed)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Panamanian S.A.; the articles typically declare authorized ordinary capital of US$10,000.00 divided into non-par-value shares. No escrow account or capital-deposit requirement exists for formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned incorporator, having issued and recorded the subscription of Share Number One of the authorized capital stock, convenes the First Board of Directors' Meeting. RESOLVED: (1) The subscription and issuance of one ordinary share to the founding shareholder is approved and entered in the share ledger; (2) The registered office is fixed at the commercial address in Panama City, Republic of Panama; (3) The following officers are appointed: President, Treasurer, and Corporate Secretary; (4) The appointed officers are jointly authorized to open corporate bank accounts, execute affiliate media-buying and lead-generation agreements, and file all statutory returns with the Public Registry and tax authorities. All resolutions were passed unanimously and are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — online name search/reservation portal (Pandeportes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three (3) proposed corporate names via the Registro Público online filing system; pay the US$50.00 name-search/reservation fee; obtain the reservation certificate valid for thirty (30) days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is refused as confusingly similar to an existing registration, re-submit an alternative reserved name within the thirty-day validity period; no substantive cure is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator or appointed representative executes the Escritura Pública de Constitución before a Panamanian Notary Public; the notary authenticates signatures and records the corporate name, registered office, capital structure and first directors in the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any notarial observation by executing a corrective addendum (aclaración) to the deed before presentation to the Registro Público.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Mercantile Division (Personas Jurídicas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed together with the prescribed registry filing form; pay the US$350.00 registration fee; the registry assigns a microfiche number and issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Certificado de Registro).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry files a defect (observación) noting omissions or inconsistencies, correct the deed by addendum and re-file within the statutory response term; expedite via the registry's e-Registro digital channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Agent Appointment and Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney / registered agent (abogado residente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint a licensed attorney as resident agent; open the corporate minute book and share ledger (Libro de Actas y Registro de Acciones) with the agent's attestation; maintain custody of the corporate seal and minute book at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If corporate books are rejected for formatting non-compliance, obtain new standardized ledgers from the licensed agent and re-certify them before the first board meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Autoridad Nacional de Gobierno Digital (AIG)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 10-RUC at the DGI to obtain the tax identification number (RUC); procure the corporate digital certificate (firma digital) through AIG for e-filing; register under the territorial-tax regime with economic activity aligned to ISIC 7310 / advertising media buying.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is deferred, present the original notarized deed to the DGI taxpayer service window and comply with any identity verification request; resolve discrepancies on site.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Operational Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Dirección de Industrias y Comercio (Aviso de Operación window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal Aviso de Operación for the registered commercial address (office-based media buying; no physical industrial plant); align the declared economic activity with ISIC 7310 digital advertising and affiliate lead generation; keep the Aviso displayed at the premises.
required_dossiers: Lease or title deed of commercial premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires additional land-use or zoning verification for the office address, complete the municipal zoning clearance and re-submit the Aviso de Operación application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Industrias; industrial manufacturing license not applicable to digital media-buying services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice) — sufficient for office-based affiliate media buying; no Manufacturing License required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category No. 3 (service/information-technology activities); no EIA study, registration, or environmental impact statement required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; zero industrial discharge. Office operations must comply with municipal solid-waste disposal ordinances; no wastewater, VOC or combustion emissions generated by the digital advertising business.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection certificate issued by the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for the commercial office space; occupational health and workplace clearance per Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) — Consejo Nacional de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional (CONASE) rules; electrical and structural load inspections certified for the leased premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; official taxpayer self-service portal: Sede Electrónica e-Tax at https://etax.mef.gob.pa; institutional website: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign legal entity deriving Panamanian-source income or performing taxable services in Panama must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) before issuing invoices or filing returns. Procedure: (1) file apostilled corporate existence documents with the Registro Público de Panamá, appoint a resident agent, and, if operating through a local branch, register the branch (Matrícula de Agencia); (2) file the municipal Aviso de Operación in the relevant corregimiento; (3) complete DGI RUC registration through the e-Tax portal using an accredited accountant or legal representative, including fiscal domicile declaration and foreign address details; (4) receive the RUC certificate and e-Tax user credentials. A foreign entity without a permanent establishment may register as a non-resident taxpayer (Contribuyente No Domiciliado) with a designated local fiscal representative. Estimated processing time: 2–4 weeks; the same RUC serves as the ITBMS VAT registration number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: Panamanian-source income is subject to corporate income tax (ISR), while foreign-source income is exempt. A Sociedad Anónima is a full entity-level taxpayer for ISR and ITBMS and is not eligible for pass-through treatment; no check-the-box mechanism exists. Dividends paid from foreign-source income remain outside Panamanian dividend withholding taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama provides no US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. Available statutory elections: (a) simplified small taxpayer regime under Law 41 of 2017 for annual gross sales below USD 10 million, with an optional final tax of 2.5% of gross sales; (b) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying headquarters services; (c) election to treat cross-border services to a non-resident recipient as zero-rated ITBMS export services where the use/benefit test is met; (d) election to distribute dividends out of declared legal reserves to apply the 5% dividend withholding rate instead of 10%; (e) application to the DGI for advance rulings/agreements confirming export zero-rating treatment for digital advertising services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS), governed by Gabinete Decree No. 11 of 1985, as amended.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de-minimis economic threshold: every Panamanian S.A. is legally required to register as an ITBMS taxpayer in the RUC before conducting its first taxable transaction. An elective simplified regime (RSPC/small taxpayer aggregation) is available where annual gross sales or imports remain below USD 10 million; above that threshold, full monthly ITBMS filing applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama's electronic invoicing system (Facturación Electrónica) is mandatory in phased tranches under DGI Resolution No. 201-5723 of 2019 and implementing regulations. Large taxpayers (generally those with gross annual income above USD 10 million) must issue electronic invoices through DGI-authorized software or the DGI e-Tax portal, incorporating a DGI digital stamp/QR code, and transmit the XML invoice data to the DGI within 24 hours of issuance. Smaller taxpayers may apply for voluntary electronic issuance or use authorized fiscal printing systems until their mandatory phase begins. Monthly ITBMS reconciliation is filed on Form 291; failure to issue or transmit electronic invoices can trigger RUC suspension and administrative fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Gabinete Decree No. 11 of 1985 and DGI interpretations, a 0% ITBMS rate applies to: (a) physical exports of goods where title passes to a non-resident buyer and the goods leave Panamanian customs territory; (b) services rendered to a beneficial user who is a non-resident without a Panamanian permanent establishment, provided the service is effectively used, exploited, or has its economic effect outside Panama; and (c) qualifying services of exportation, including performance-marketing and digital advertising media buying, where the campaigns target non-Panama audiences under contract with a foreign advertiser and are paid for from foreign bank accounts. Eligibility is substantive rather than formal: the exporter must prove the foreign beneficiary's residency, the export contract, the invoicing chain, and cross-border settlement; where the advertisement benefit is deemed to accrue in Panama, 7% ITBMS applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Exportación via SIGA/ANA) or DGI-recognized export certificate
Transport document: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (Conocimiento de Embarque) evidencing the foreign consignee and actual departure from Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Remesa del Banco / SWIFT MT103) proving cross-border payment from the non-resident client
Commercial invoice, purchase order, service agreement, and performance metrics (ad server/geolocation reports) identifying the foreign beneficiary
Signed affidavit or certificate of non-use in Panama confirming that the service benefit accrued outside Panamanian territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama has no foreign-exchange controls or statutory FX repatriation deadline; the Balboa is at par with the USD and the economy is dollarized. However, DGI audits export zero-rating claims through exporter-focused fiscalization programs. Where export zero-rating is unjustified or fraudulently claimed: (a) the underlying ITBMS is retroactively assessed at 7% on the full consideration; (b) a late-payment recargo of 50% of the tax due may be imposed; (c) default interest accrues from the original due date; (d) fines range from 100% to 300% of the omitted tax for inaccurate or false returns; (e) the RUC may be suspended and the exporter authorization revoked; (f) criminal tax fraud (defraudación tributaria) under Law 76 of 2019 may apply, carrying imprisonment from 2 to 5 years, extended to 5–8 years where the evasion exceeds USD 1 million or involves organized criminal structures; (g) the case may be referred to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under Law 23 of 2015 for anti-money-laundering investigation, with asset freezing and secondary penalties for assisting professionals.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no central bank. Bank supervision and prudential regulation are exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and payment agent for the State, but does not perform traditional central bank monetary functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama uses the United States Dollar as legal tender alongside the Panamanian Balboa at a 1:1 par relationship. There are no exchange control laws, no restrictions on current account or capital account transactions, and no government approval requirement for inbound or outbound fund transfers. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, loan repayments, and capital repatriation are fully convertible and free from FX-specific barriers; however, all flows remain subject to standard AML/CFT cancellation, beneficial ownership verification, and documentary source-of-funds requirements imposed by licensed banks and the SBP. Panamanian withholding or dividend tax obligations apply independently of FX remittance rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: N/A — Panama imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirement. Exporters may retain proceeds in USD or any freely convertible currency in any authorised bank account. Receipts from affiliate media buying and digital advertising services are treated as operational inflows and must be supported by underlying contracts, invoices, and traffic/performance reports for banking compliance purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility as an ancillary clearing layer only. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Mercury, and Payoneer do not hold Panamanian banking licences and cannot lawfully take deposits from, or provide principal clearing account services to, a Panamanian corporation without an SBP authorisation. They may be used for supplementary receivable collection or international vendor disbursements where their operating legislation permits inbound and outbound wires, but funds must ultimately be settled into an account at a Panamanian licensed bank for legal substance and AML credibility. Legal constraints under Law 23 of 2015 require full traceability, robust verification of beneficial owners, and no unnamed payee or account-number-only flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Panamanian banking practice is not uniform. Generally, at least one director and the final beneficial owner / authorised signatory must provide a certified signature before a Panamanian notary or a bank compliance officer. Several SBP-regulated banks permit remote onboarding using apostilled and legalised corporate documents provided the file is instructed through a registered resident agent; the ultimate signatory may, at the bank's discretion, be required to attend an in-person or video interview. A certified resolution of the board of directors authorising the account is always mandatory, and the acceptance of remote attendance depends on the bank's internal risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity matching multiple affiliate payouts to numerous small publisher networks and lead-generation vendors in a short period.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; master affiliate agreements; independent publisher contracts; payout reconciliation ledger; ad-platform invoice records (Google, Meta, TikTok, Bing); traffic statistics from verified UX/click-data providers; annual financial statements; local tax filings; and a compliance memorandum documenting the commercial logic of each payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution originating from a high-risk or reputational-risk jurisdiction with an opaque source of wealth explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters for the shareholders, notarised and apostilled source-of-wealth statement, audited financial statements of the beneficial owner, shareholder registry extract, board resolution approving the capital injection, and any trust or corporate ownership diagrams proving ultimate individual ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate structure displaying no physical office, no employees, and reliance solely on a registered agent, causing a failure of substance verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered address and term of occupancy, service agreement with the local agent, moulded organisational chart showing directors and any staff, employment contracts where applicable, corporate profile summary, and a written description of management and decision-making control over the media buying campaign assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or negative press regarding the company, its directors, or its connected advertisers referencing suspected fraud, prohibited content, or involvement in illegal online schemes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC risk-rating report, reputational search results from a professional screening provider, sworn declarations from directors, remedial compliance procedures, third-party audit of advertising inventory / publisher onboarding, and evidence of valid data protection and consumer consent mechanisms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital transfers must be executed by SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's own bank account to the Panama-domiciled corporate operational or escrow account at a licensed bank. The remitee must use a clear purpose identifier in SWIFT field 70, e.g., 'Capital Contribution' or 'Aporte de Capital', and the wire amount must match the bank-approved account mandate. The Panama corporation must provide the shareholder resolution approving the contribution, a copy of the share registry entry (Registro de Accionistas), and a source-of-funds declaration if the transfer exceeds the bank's AML threshold. There is no central bank conversion approval or foreign investment registration required in Panama, but the receiving bank will conduct a documentary compliance review and may request evidence of the underlying commercial purpose.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border trade settlements related to digital advertising and affiliate commissions, the standard clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for single supplier wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) where the vendor requires bank-to-bank settlement security. Payments to major ad platforms and publishers are ordinarily sent via SWIFT using the corporate account's correspondent banking network in the United States, with local Panamanian US-dollar clearing also available through the national ACH and RTGS systems for domestic payments. No foreign exchange authorization is required for outbound payments; banks apply standard SBP AML checks and may require the presentation of invoices, media buy agreements, traffic reports, or platform statements to evidence the commercial nature of the disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/EUR and other major currency pairs through SBP-licensed banks
Cross-currency swaps for legally committed non-USD liabilities such as vendor payables and overseas payroll
Vanilla call and put foreign-exchange options traded bilaterally with licensed Panamanian or foreign counterparties
Collateralised spot-forward combinations used to fix the USD cost of future non-USD ad inventory contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax Declaration and Payment (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 15 each calendar year for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: USD 50 late-filing penalty; monthly interest of 1% on the unpaid tax; administrative strike-off and dissolution if unpaid for three consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 15 together with the franchise tax payment; interim update required within 15 days of any ownership or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from USD 100 to USD 10,000 under Law 23 of 2015 (AML); possible suspension of commercial registration for repeat non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual gross revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 or total assets exceed USD 500,000; also mandatory for banks, insurance companies, and securities issuers
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public interest entities; IFRS for SMEs or local accounting principles (DPC) for private companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: File a sworn annual declaration identifying all ultimate beneficial owners, nationalities, residency status, and percentage of direct/indirect participation. Transfer of shares during the year must be reflected in the declaration and updated in the Beneficial Ownership Registry within 15 calendar days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute for a private S.A. below the audit threshold; voluntary certified audit typical range USD 2,500 – USD 5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (flat corporate rate under Law 8 of 2010; a 15% preferential rate applies to the first B/. 50,000 of taxable income for small taxpayers under the 2019 progressive scale, provided total taxable income does not exceed B/. 50,000).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial tax system: only Panamanian-source income is subject to corporate income tax, while foreign-source income (e.g., affiliate commissions from foreign ad networks where negotiation, contract execution and service performance occur outside Panama) is exempt, provided it is properly documented. No statutory tax holidays or media-sector incentives apply to ISIC 7310 affiliate media buying; the small-taxpayer 15% bracket is the only preferential deduction mechanism available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Declaración Jurada del Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed electronically via the DGI e-Tax 2.0 / SIT portal (Sistema Integrado de Tributación) or through an authorized registered accountant; filings are linked to the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 200), supplemented by mandatory monthly provisional payments through Form 206 (Pago Directo) at 2% of gross monthly income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year entities, Form 200 is due by 15 April of the following fiscal year, subject to the annual DGI filing calendar assigned by the last digit of the RUC; for non-calendar fiscal years, the return is due within three months and fifteen days after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique taxpayer identification number and verification digit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the entity's Panamanian RUC only; foreign shareholders are not identified on Form 200.
Use ISIC 7310 (Advertising) for affiliate media buying and lead generation; NAICS 541810 may be recorded in supporting schedules only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line A - Ingresos de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from Panamanian-source activities, including services physically rendered in Panama or sales to Panamanian counterparties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Panama-source turnover. Cross-border affiliate commissions paid by foreign advertising networks are generally excluded as foreign-source income where the contract, negotiation and execution occur outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line B - Ingresos de Fuente Extranjera (Exentos)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source gross revenue exempt under Panama's territorial tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be substantiated by contracts, site-of-performance evidence, board minutes and bank statements; aggressive attribution of Panama-executed digital work as foreign income invites DGI recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line C - Costos y Gastos Deducibles
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly attributable to Panamanian-source gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Media-buying traffic acquisition costs, sub-affiliate commissions and SaaS software fees are deductible only against Panama-source income and only with valid invoices and transfer pricing support; foreign overhead unrelated to Panama-source income is disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% rate (15% on the first B/. 50,000 if the small-taxpayer threshold applies) and reconcile the result with the transfer pricing annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line E - Impuesto Determinado y Créditos
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at 25%, credited against monthly Pago Directo payments at 2% of gross monthly income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show balance due or credit carry-forward; no foreign tax credit is available on exempt foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing annex and transactional schedules required when related-party transactions occur or the B/. 2.5 million revenue threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all controlled transactions with foreign affiliates, including intercompany commissions, media-buying rebates and software licensing fees, with arm's length benchmarking; attach Local File / Master File where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a default surcharge of 1.5% per month on the tax due, capped at 20%, plus statutory monthly interest of 1.5%; flat administrative fines range from B/. 250 to B/. 10,000. Persistent non-compliance may result in suspension of the Certificado de Solvencia Fiscal, preventive embargo of bank accounts, restriction of Registro Público filings, and denial of DGI clearance certificates for corporate dissolution or resident agent changes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid, credited or distributed by a Panamanian S.A. out of Panamanian-source taxed profits; the rate increases to 20% for distributions to bearer-share holders where beneficial ownership is not disclosed. Dividends paid out of exempt foreign-source profits can be repatriated without dividend WHT only if the exemption is properly reflected in Form 200 and audited books.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a limited DTA network (Barbados, Mexico, the Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, Spain, South Korea, UAE). To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the home tax authority, (ii) provide legalized/apostilled TRC plus a declaration of beneficial ownership to the Panamanian paying entity, and (iii) ensure the paying entity files the corresponding informational return with the DGI referencing the treaty article. Reduced rates apply only where the shareholder meets the DTA's beneficial-ownership and holding-period conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 12.5% WHT on Panamanian-source IP payments (trademarks, software, digital assets); treaty rates range from 0% to 10% depending on the DTA (e.g., 10% under Panama-Netherlands). Interest: 0% WHT for interest paid to bona fide foreign banking institutions; otherwise up to 12.5% WHT on Panamanian-source interest paid to non-residents, reduced to 0%-5% under selected DTAs and subject to earnings-stripping/arm's length analysis.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 2,500,000 (Balboa, pegged 1:1 to USD) in annual gross operating revenue triggers mandatory Local File documentation; Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue above USD 10,000,000; controlled transactions exceeding B/. 250,000 require transactional filing schedules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR, Law 254 of 2023 and DGI implementing guidance) require a Panama-resident S.A. engaged in a relevant activity, including digital advertising and affiliate media buying as a service business, to maintain prescribed economic substance in Panama: physical office premises, locally employed qualified staff proportionate to the activity, real operating expenditure, local board/management minutes, and an annual substance declaration filed with the DGI. A pure mailbox affiliate buyer with no local substance and decision-making conducted abroad may be classified as a shell company, lose the territorial exemption for foreign-source income, be subject to recharacterization of income as Panamanian-source, and face deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting Panamanian-source media-buying revenue from Form 200, inflating affiliate traffic acquisition costs through circular or fictitious invoicing, or diverting ACH/Wise/wire receipts into personal or offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal Code administrative surcharge of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax plus 1.5% monthly default interest; criminal tax fraud under the Penal Code carries imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and monetary fines where the evaded amount exceeds B/. 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or authorize false returns are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt; courts may impose preventive asset embargoes, travel bans, disqualification from holding office in Panamanian entities, and imprisonment upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a mailbox S.A. with no physical office in Panama, no locally authorized employees, no real activity or expenditure, use of nominee shareholders without disclosed beneficial owners, and failure to file the annual economic substance declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR fines of up to B/. 50,000 per fiscal period; administrative recharacterization of formerly exempt foreign-source income as Panamanian-source, exposing the full profit to 25% corporate tax plus interest; cancellation of the operating license and strike-off from the Registro Público.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent are personally liable for knowingly submitting false substance declarations; sanctions include debarment from acting as resident agents, monetary fines, and criminal liability for perjury or false affidavit where the declaration is used to deceive the DGI or foreign tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving affiliate commissions through cryptocurrency or unverified payment rails, paying sub-affiliates via omnibus accounts, or failing to maintain client due diligence, beneficial ownership records, and transaction monitoring in a money-services-risk business model.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under the Penal Code is punishable by imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and fines; UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) administrative penalties may reach B/. 2,000,000; funds are subject to freezing and forfeiture, and affected bank accounts may be closed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and the designated Compliance Officer (OFC) face personal criminal prosecution for failures in filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (ROS), implementing the AML manual, or identifying ultimate beneficial owners; travel restrictions and disqualification from financial or corporate roles apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying foreign related affiliates commissions, software licensing fees, or media-buying rebates above arm's length; absence of a Local File or benchmarking study; failure to file the transfer pricing annex to Form 200.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may make a transfer pricing adjustment increasing Panamanian-source taxable income, impose an additional 40% surcharge on the deficiency, charge 1.5% monthly default interest, and levy fines up to B/. 10,000 for missing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve unsubstantiated intercompany pricing and leave the Panamanian entity undercapitalized may be personally assessed for the transfer pricing deficiency and associated interest if the S.A. is liquidated, insolvent, or found to have disregarded corporate formalities.
